overview_text: Apple designs, manufactures, and markets iPhone, Mac, iPad, wearables, and services (App Store, iCloud, Apple Music, etc.). This snapshot uses real publicly reported data gathered via web search on 2026-08-02, not a live data feed, so treat exact intraday figures as approximate where noted below. Apple reported record fiscal Q3 2026 (June quarter) results on 2026-07-30 — its outgoing CEO Tim Cook's final earnings call before transitioning to executive chairman on 2026-09-01, handing the CEO role to John Ternus (SVP of Hardware Engineering, ~25-year Apple veteran). Despite beating estimates on revenue and EPS, shares fell roughly 7% the next trading day on weak forward guidance and a Services/Greater China miss.

news_digest_last_6.headline: Apple earnings takeaways: Weak forecast, supply concerns overshadow sales beat in Cook's last report as CEO
Apple iPhone sales shine, but services segment and China revenue misses estimates
Apple forecasts slower sales growth as chip supply crunch persists
Apple Loses No. 1 Market Cap Over Memory Crunch, Eyes Chinese Chips
Apple Q3 FY26: Record Quarter, Weak Guidance, Siri Timing
Apple Enters The Ternus Era As Investors Weigh Its Next Innovation Cycle

risks_notes_text: Guidance deceleration: management guided September-quarter (Q4 FY26) revenue growth to just 9-11% YoY, down sharply from the 16% just reported, citing a 2.5pp FX headwind and increased supply constraints on iPhone/Mac/iPad. Margin pressure: gross margin guided down to 47-48% (from 48.65% TTM) due to sharply rising memory-chip costs, which Tim Cook himself called a 'hundred-year flood' — severe enough that Apple already raised Mac/iPad prices in June 2026. Double miss in two strategic growth vectors: Services revenue ($30.74B, +12.1% YoY) and Greater China revenue ($18.82B, +22.4% YoY) both grew but missed analyst estimates. Leadership transition risk: Tim Cook hands the CEO role to John Ternus on 2026-09-01 — Ternus's first quarter in charge will be the one guided down; analysts are described as taking a 'wait and see' stance on whether he can revive Apple's innovation cycle. Valuation: trailing P/E of ~40x is well above Apple's own historical norm (typically 25-30x) and prices in continued AI-driven monetization (revamped Siri built with Google/Alphabet, expanded Apple Intelligence unveiled at WWDC 2026) — a real earnings disappointment during the leadership handoff could compress this multiple materially. Notable tension in the data: several sell-side analysts (Wedbush, Bank of America, Evercore ISI) raised price targets into the $365-400 range around/after this report citing the AI roadmap, even as the stock itself fell ~7% and lost its #1 market-cap ranking — i.e., near-term price action and longer-term sell-side sentiment are currently pulling in opposite directions. Offsetting strength: balance sheet remains very strong ($146.5B cash/marketable securities vs. $84.3B debt), giving real cushion and buyback capacity through the transition.
